title: Republicans, Democrats continue to differ sharply on voting access
summary: About six-in-ten Americans support no-excuse early or absentee voting, but partisan divides remain, with GOP support falling sharply since 2018.

title: Video: How to spot a good poll vs. a bad poll
summary: Anyone can ask a survey question online – but does that make it a good poll? They might call themselves a pollster, but their methods aren’t exactly best practice — and the internet is flooded with these low-quality polls. Here are a few simple things you can look for to tell whether a poll is legit or sketchy.

title: For Working Parents, the Boundary Between Work and Family Is Often Blurred
summary: Parents – especially moms – often carry the mental load that comes with trying to balance what their families need with what their job demands. And with so many obligations, it’s not surprising that working parents sometimes feel like they can’t give 100% at home or at work.

title: How workplace benefits and flexibility shape parents’ ability to balance work and family
summary: As part of a larger survey about their experiences, we asked working parents what work arrangements or employer-provided benefits would be the most helpful to them and whether those things are available at their current job. summary: As many workers face return-to-office mandates, some parents have been able to maintain remote or hybrid work arrangements. title: How working parents divide family responsibilities
summary: To understand how different-sex couples share household and parenting tasks when both parents have full-time jobs, we asked parents in this type of family who does more when it comes to these responsibilities. The data shows that, in families with a mother and a father, moms often take on more of the load. Read more […]

title: How family work arrangements have changed over time
summary: The work arrangements of moms and dads who are married or living together have changed considerably in recent decades. As of 2025, just over half (52%) of different-sex couples with children under 18 consist of two full-time working parents. This is up from 46% a decade ago and 31% in 1975, according to Pew Research […]

More Countries Had Elevated Levels of Social Hostilities Involving Religion in 2023
summary: The number of countries with high or very high social hostilities rose for the third year in a row; government interference in worship also increased.

title: Number of countries with high or very high social hostilities rose in 2023
summary: The six countries with very high social hostilities involving religion were Nigeria, India, Israel, Syria, Bangladesh and Pakistan.

title: Harassment of religious groups around the world in 2023
summary: Religious groups faced harassment in 192 of 198 countries and territories, matching a previous high from 2022.

title: Restrictions on religion rose in most regions in 2023 but declined in sub-Saharan Africa
summary: Median levels of government restrictions and social hostilities rose in Europe, Asia and the Pacific, and the Middle East and North Africa.

title: Religious restrictions in the 25 most populous countries in 2023
summary: India, Egypt, Pakistan, Iran and Indonesia ranked highest in overall levels of government restrictions on religion and social hostilities.

title: For the 100th anniversary of the SAT, a look at standardized test scores over time
summary: As the SAT nears its 100th anniversary, here's a look at how the test has changed since 1926 and how scores on both the SAT and ACT have shifted over time.

title: More than half of states will recognize Juneteenth as a legal holiday in 2026
summary: This year, at least 33 states and the District of Columbia will legally recognize Juneteenth as a public holiday.

title: Americans are more dissatisfied with how their democracy is working than people in other high-income countries
summary: A large majority of Democrats (86%) are dissatisfied with how American democracy is working. Around half of Republicans (51%) say the same.

title: Political Typology
summary: Political Typology The political typology uses survey data to classify the American public into nine political groups based on responses to 30 questions about their political values and beliefs. title: Beyond Red vs. Blue: The Political Typology
summary: Our typology sorts the public into nine groups based on their political and cultural values, not their party – painting a picture of American politics with far more than two colors.
